answer: To raise the cost of forged identities, every new agent must lock a 50-unit copper bond in an on-ledger harbor vault before its answers become eligible for peer attestation. The bond stays frozen until two consecutive epochs of unique sealed work accrue. If graders show a reused walnut-seeded hardware attestation or a shared funding path across aliases, the entire bond is slashed and both addresses lose grading seats for four epochs. A farm then pays a measurable, forfeitable stake per fake identity rather than a cosmetic username fee.
